item.title: [IGNITE-1619] Platform .Net: Generic type is lost during array/collection serialization
item.description:
We do not serialize collection/array element type, so on deserialization we can not recreate original collection. So generic arrays/collections can't be used in job arguments, service arguments, etc.

  • We should keep current format for non-generic collections, arrays of primitives, and arrays of objects
  • Generic collections and arrays should be written with new TypeIds (not compatible with other platforms) and include type information

Done.
Removed generic collection support in PortableBuilder (exception is thrown).
Xmldoc updated (only non-generic collections, primitive arrays and object arrays can be used for interop).

Partial review of public API:
1) Looks like WriteObjectArray should be split into pair of methods for consistency with collections/dictionaries and to avoid misuse: WriteObjectArray(object[]) and WriteGenericObjectArray<T>(T[]).

Lets fix that and add new metadata types and finish with public part. Protocol implementation can be reviewed independenty.

There is another problem with this ticket: adding TypeId that is not supported in Java can break Compute API and other things if user decides to use one of these onsupported types as a Job argument, for example. Java part won't be able to pass it around.

Let's stop this ticket until we have an ability to pass around unsopported types in Java.
Instead of supporting additional type id in Java, we can wrap any .Net-specific things in a portable wrapper (same way as we do with Serializables).
WriteGeneric*/ReadGeneric* methods removed from API. Let's keep specialized methods for interop. All other things go through WriteObject.

Pavel, my comments:
1) Public API - why did we remove <T> from WriteArray/ReadArray methods?
2) PortableWriterImpl: It is not clear why do we lookup generic collection descriptor from PortableCollectionInfo, while we can re-use PortableSystemHandlers?

Pavel,
My comments:
1) IPortable()Raw)Writer: "Write non-generic collection." - this method is to write collection in portable form, not to write "non-generic".
2) IPortable(Raw)Reader: "Only non-generic collections can be used for interop with other platforms." - this is not true, any collection can be used for interop.
3) CollectionHolder: "writer.WriteBoolean(desc.UserType);" - why do we write this flag?
4) PortableUtils: why collection and map types are removed?
5) Collection write logic is extremely slow. Most of the things can be done only once when we first met collection of that type. Let's keep it is as is for now to speed merge, but new ticket must be created right away to optimize it.
6) CollectionHolder.WriteType(): "var desc = writer.Marshaller.GetDescriptor(type);" - looks incorrect to me. If we have a descriptor for collection, we should not even reach this place, are we?

Since most CLR collections are Serializable, we can rely on that instead of inventing our own mechanism.
The downside is that elements of List<UserPortableMarshalAware> will be written as Serializable instead of Portable, but user can work around that by serializing the collection manually.

1,2) Comments fixed
3,5,6) Removed, no more applicable
4) Reverted

1) PortableBuilderImpl: looks like ThrowIfGenericCollection should be removed, no need for this check. Is it?
2) Missing if-branch for "CollectionHashSet" in PortableUtils.ReadCollection/WriteCollection methods.
3) Missing docs for readers.

1,3) Fixed
2) HashSet<T> does not implement ICollection, so we can't use it in these methods. There is no non-generic set in .Net.
